biodiversity_overview.text: 15,856 GBIF occurrence records for 52 tracked species are attributed to Delhi, spanning 1877-2026.
15,653 of these records (98.7%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 24, Mammalia 10, Magnoliopsida 9, Squamata 4, Testudines 3, Amphibia 1, Actinopterygii 1.

threatened_species.text: 5 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Grey-Hornbill (2,360), Indian Pied Starling (2,246), Common Peafowl (1,889), Indian White-eye (1,658), White-throated Munia (1,585).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,077 in 2016 to 241 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.77% of Delhi's area (2 areas intersect the state).
8.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (1,286 of 15,653); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Courser (0.47), Indian Tent Turtle (0.44), Indian Gooseberry (0.35).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Delhi (equal-weight reference): cell near 28.875N 76.875E (overall rank 40, median rank across weightings 58).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 3 km2 (0.18% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

0.1 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (4.73% of the 2000 extent; 0.0% in 2015-2024, rank 33 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2007 (0.03 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 19.71% of land and population density is 13,771.1 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
92% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
